from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Hook: The Disputed Treasure"
        lines = [
            "Alice and Bob must share a stolen necklace fairly.",
            "It has different types of precious beads.",
            "How many cuts guarantee each gets half of every type?"
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Alice (#FFD700) and Bob (#87CEEB) icons appear with a necklace
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Alice Icon (Simplified Person)
        alice_head = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1)
        alice_body = Triangle(color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.4).next_to(alice_head, DOWN, buff=0.05)
        alice_label = Text("Alice", font_size=16, color="#FFD700").next_to(alice_head, UP, buff=0.1)
        alice_icon = VGroup(alice_head, alice_body, alice_label)
        self.place_at_grid(alice_icon, "A2", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Bob Icon (Simplified Person)
        bob_head = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#87CEEB", fill_opacity=1)
        bob_body = Triangle(color="#87CEEB", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.4).next_to(bob_head, DOWN, buff=0.05)
        bob_label = Text("Bob", font_size=16, color="#87CEEB").next_to(bob_head, UP, buff=0.1)
        bob_icon = VGroup(bob_head, bob_body, bob_label)
        self.place_at_grid(bob_icon, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Necklace Construction
        necklace_line = Line(self.grid["B1"], self.grid["B6"], color=GREY_A, stroke_width=2)
        # Sequence with 10 Red and 8 Green
        colors = ["#FF0000", "#00FF00", "#FF0000", "#FF0000", "#00FF00", 
                  "#00FF00", "#FF0000", "#FF0000", "#FF0000", "#00FF00", 
                  "#FF0000", "#00FF00", "#FF0000", "#FF0000", "#00FF00", 
                  "#00FF00", "#00FF00", "#FF0000"]
        
        beads = VGroup()
        for i, color in enumerate(colors):
            dot = Dot(radius=0.12, color=color, fill_opacity=1)
            dot.move_to(necklace_line.point_from_proportion(i/17))
            beads.add(dot)
        
        necklace_full = VGroup(necklace_line, beads)

        self.play(FadeIn(alice_icon), FadeIn(bob_icon))
        self.play(Create(necklace_line), LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(b) for b in beads], lag_ratio=0.05))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The necklace is labeled 'Stolen Necklace' and beads are counted: '10 Red, 8 Green'.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        stolen_text = Text("Stolen Necklace", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(stolen_text, "C1", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        count_text = Text("10 Red, 8 Green", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(count_text, "D1", "D6", scale_factor=0.9)
        # Apply colors to counts
        count_text[0:2].set_color("#FF0000") # "10"
        count_text[3:6].set_color("#FF0000") # "Red"
        count_text[8:9].set_color("#00FF00") # "8"
        count_text[10:].set_color("#00FF00") # "Green"

        self.play(Write(stolen_text))
        self.play(Write(count_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A question mark appears next to a knife: 'How many cuts for a fair split?'.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Knife graphic
        knife_handle = Rectangle(height=0.1, width=0.4, color="#8B4513", fill_opacity=1)
        knife_blade = Triangle(color="#C0C0C0", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.3).rotate(-90*DEGREES)
        knife_blade.next_to(knife_handle, RIGHT, buff=0)
        knife = VGroup(knife_handle, knife_blade).rotate(45*DEGREES)
        
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=60, color=YELLOW)
        knife_group = VGroup(knife, question_mark).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(knife_group, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(knife_group))
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Prerequisite: The Intermediate Value Theorem (1D Case)"
        lines = [
            "Imagine a necklace with only one type of bead.",
            "Sliding a knife from start to end changes the share.",
            "The Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a perfect 50/50 cut."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        RED_BEAD = "#FF0000"
        KNIFE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a necklace of red beads
        self.lecture[0].set_color(RED_BEAD)
        
        necklace_string = Line(start=self.grid['A1'], end=self.grid['A6'], color=GREY_A)
        beads = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.12, color=RED_BEAD, fill_opacity=1).move_to(
                necklace_string.point_from_proportion(i / 10)
            ) for i in range(11)
        ])
        necklace = VGroup(necklace_string, beads)
        
        self.play(Create(necklace))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Create Axes for the plot
        self.lecture[1].set_color(KNIFE_COLOR)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1, 0.5],
            y_range=[0, 100, 50],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20},
            tips=False
        )
        x_label = Text("Cut Position", font_size=16).next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN)
        y_label = Text("Alice's %", font_size=16).next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT).rotate(90 * DEGREES)
        plot_group = VGroup(axes, x_label, y_label)
        self.place_in_area(plot_group, 'C2', 'F5')
        
        # Knife object
        knife_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        knife = Line(
            start=self.grid['A1'] + UP * 0.5,
            end=self.grid['A1'] + DOWN * 0.5,
            color=KNIFE_COLOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        # Function for the share: simple linear 0 to 100
        def get_share_line():
            val = knife_tracker.get_value()
            return axes.plot(lambda x: 100 * x, x_range=[0, val], color=RED_BEAD)

        plot_line = always_redraw(get_share_line)
        
        # Add updater to knife to follow tracker
        knife.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            interpolate(self.grid['A1'], self.grid['A6'], knife_tracker.get_value())
        ))

        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.add(knife, plot_line)
        
        # Slide knife from 0 to 1
        self.play(knife_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Reset knife to 0.5 to show the 50/50 point
        self.play(knife_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=2)
        
        # Highlight point on graph
        target_point = axes.c2p(0.5, 50)
        highlight_dot = Dot(target_point, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, radius=0.1)
        
        # Guidelines to axes
        h_line = axes.get_horizontal_line(target_point, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        v_line = axes.get_vertical_line(target_point, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Labels for 50%
        label_50 = Text("50%", font_size=18, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR).next_to(h_line, LEFT)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(highlight_dot, scale=0.5),
            Create(h_line),
            Create(v_line),
            Write(label_50)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(highlight_dot, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with specific lines
        title = "The Core Concept: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem"
        lines = [
            "The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem addresses continuous maps on spheres.",
            "Every map from a sphere to space has antipodal matches.",
            "Antipodal points are exactly opposite on the sphere.",
            "These points map to the exact same value.",
            "On Earth, two opposite spots share temperature and pressure."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Color definitions
        COL_L1 = BLUE_B
        COL_L2 = BLUE_A
        COL_L3 = RED
        COL_L4 = WHITE
        COL_L5 = GREEN_B

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Sphere (S2) visual representation (stylized 2D sphere)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COL_L1))
        
        sphere_bg = Circle(radius=1.5, color=COL_L1, fill_opacity=0.1)
        equator = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=0.6, color=COL_L1, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        meridian = Ellipse(width=0.6, height=3.0, color=COL_L1, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        sphere_group = VGroup(sphere_bg, equator, meridian)
        
        self.place_in_area(sphere_group, "B2", "E5")
        sphere_center = sphere_group.get_center()
        
        self.play(Create(sphere_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COL_L2))
        # Visualizing a map 'f' from Sn to Rn conceptually (using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency)
        f_label = Text("f: Sⁿ → ℝⁿ", color=COL_L2)
        self.place_at_grid(f_label, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(f_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COL_L3))
        
        # Antipodal points x and -x
        angle = PI / 4
        p1_coord = sphere_center + np.array([1.5 * np.cos(angle), 1.5 * np.sin(angle), 0])
        p2_coord = sphere_center + np.array([1.5 * np.cos(angle + PI), 1.5 * np.sin(angle + PI), 0])
        
        dot1 = Dot(p1_coord, color=COL_L3)
        dot2 = Dot(p2_coord, color=COL_L3)
        
        label_x = Text("x", color=COL_L3, slant=ITALIC, font_size=24).next_to(dot1, UR, buff=0.1)
        label_mx = Text("-x", color=COL_L3, slant=ITALIC, font_size=24).next_to(dot2, DL, buff=0.1)
        
        antipodal_group = VGroup(dot1, dot2, label_x, label_mx)
        self.play(FadeIn(antipodal_group))
        
        # Show connection line to emphasize they are opposite
        line_opp = Line(p1_coord, p2_coord, color=RED, stroke_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        self.play(Create(line_opp))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COL_L4))
        
        # The main formula f(x) = f(-x)
        formula = Text("f(x) = f(-x)", color=COL_L4)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A3", "A4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COL_L5))
        
        # Earth example labels
        earth_data1 = VGroup(
            Text("Temp: 20°C", font_size=16, color=COL_L5),
            Text("Press: 1013hPa", font_size=16, color=COL_L5)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).next_to(dot1, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        earth_data2 = VGroup(
            Text("Temp: 20°C", font_size=16, color=COL_L5),
            Text("Press: 1013hPa", font_size=16, color=COL_L5)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).next_to(dot2, LEFT, buff=0.2)
        
        # Change sphere color to more Earth-like Green/Blue
        self.play(
            sphere_bg.animate.set_color(GREEN_E),
            FadeIn(earth_data1),
            FadeIn(earth_data2)
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define line colors
        line_colors = ["#FFD700", "#87CEEB", "#FFD700", "#87CEEB", "#FFD700"]
        alice_color = "#FFD700"
        bob_color = "#87CEEB"
        
        self.setup_layout(
            "Mapping the Necklace to a Sphere", 
            [
                "We can represent necklace partitions using a sphere's surface.", 
                "Each point on the sphere defines specific cut locations.", 
                "Moving to the opposite point swaps Alice and Bob's portions.", 
                "This maps the physical problem into a topological space.", 
                "The number of bead types determines the sphere's dimension."
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(line_colors[0])
        
        # Create a "necklace" made of colored dots (beads)
        bead_colors = [RED, BLUE, GREEN, RED, BLUE, GREEN, RED, BLUE]
        necklace_linear = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.1, color=c) for c in bead_colors]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(necklace_linear, "B2", "B5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(necklace_linear))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transform necklace into a circular loop (S1)
        necklace_loop = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE).set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(necklace_loop, "C2", "E5")
        
        # Create dots arranged on a circle
        beads_on_circle = VGroup()
        for i, color in enumerate(bead_colors):
            angle = i * (TAU / len(bead_colors))
            dot = Dot(radius=0.1, color=color)
            dot.move_to(necklace_loop.point_at_angle(angle))
            beads_on_circle.add(dot)
            
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(necklace_linear, beads_on_circle),
            Create(necklace_loop)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(line_colors[1])
        
        # Visual representation of a "sphere" using the circle and an ellipse for perspective
        sphere_depth = Ellipse(width=3, height=1, color=WHITE).set_stroke(opacity=0.2)
        sphere_depth.move_to(necklace_loop.get_center())
        
        # Highlighting a point on the "sphere"
        cut_point = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(necklace_loop.point_at_angle(PI/4))
        cut_label = Text("Cut Positions", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(cut_label, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        cut_label.next_to(cut_point, UR, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(sphere_depth))
        self.play(FadeIn(cut_point), Write(cut_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(line_colors[2])
        
        # Visual segments for Alice and Bob
        # We'll split the circle into two halves for simplicity in this visualization
        arc_alice = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI/4, angle=PI, color=alice_color, stroke_width=6)
        arc_bob = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI/4 + PI, angle=PI, color=bob_color, stroke_width=6)
        arc_alice.move_to(necklace_loop.get_center())
        arc_bob.move_to(necklace_loop.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(arc_alice), Create(arc_bob))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Move point to antipodal position
        antipodal_point = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(necklace_loop.point_at_angle(PI/4 + PI))
        
        # Update arcs - swapping colors
        new_arc_alice = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI/4 + PI, angle=PI, color=alice_color, stroke_width=6)
        new_arc_bob = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI/4, angle=PI, color=bob_color, stroke_width=6)
        new_arc_alice.move_to(necklace_loop.get_center())
        new_arc_bob.move_to(necklace_loop.get_center())

        self.play(
            cut_point.animate.move_to(antipodal_point.get_center()),
            cut_label.animate.next_to(antipodal_point, DL, buff=0.1),
            Transform(arc_alice, new_arc_alice),
            Transform(arc_bob, new_arc_bob)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(line_colors[3])
        
        # Visualizing the "mapping" - pulse effect on the sphere
        pulse_sphere = necklace_loop.copy().set_color(BLUE).set_stroke(width=10, opacity=0.5)
        self.play(pulse_sphere.animate.scale(1.2).set_opacity(0), run_time=1.5)
        self.remove(pulse_sphere)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(line_colors[4])
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'latex'
        dimension_text = Text("S^{k-1}", color=WHITE)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Conclusion and Real-World Intuition", 
            [
                'We proved k cuts always satisfy both thieves.', 
                'Topology transforms a complex division problem into geometry.', 
                'Math ensures fairness even in the most disputed treasures.'
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        COLOR_K = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_ALICE = "#FFC0CB" # Pink
        COLOR_BOB = "#87CEEB"   # Sky Blue
        COLOR_SPHERE = "#4444FF"
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line: "We proved k cuts always satisfy both thieves."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        summary_text = Text("k beads, k cuts", weight=BOLD, color=COLOR_K)
        self.place_in_area(summary_text, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(summary_text))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line: "Topology transforms a complex division problem into geometry."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)

        # Create a sphere (Circle with gradient) and a necklace overlay
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.2, color=COLOR_SPHERE).set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        sphere_glow = Circle(radius=1.2, color=COLOR_SPHERE).set_fill(COLOR_SPHERE, opacity=0.1)
        
        # Necklace on sphere (a great circle with beads)
        necklace_loop = Ellipse(width=2.4, height=0.6, color=WHITE).set_stroke(width=2)
        bead_colors = [RED, YELLOW, GREEN, BLUE, ORANGE, PURPLE]
        beads = VGroup(*[
            Dot(necklace_loop.point_from_proportion(i/6), color=bead_colors[i], radius=0.08)
            for i in range(6)
        ])
        
        geom_group = VGroup(sphere, sphere_glow, necklace_loop, beads)
        self.place_in_area(geom_group, "C1", "D6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Create(sphere), FadeIn(sphere_glow))
        self.play(Create(necklace_loop), FadeIn(beads))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line: "Math ensures fairness even in the most disputed treasures."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)

        # Alice and Bob Icons
        def create_person(color, label):
            head = Circle(radius=0.3, color=color, fill_opacity=0.5)
            name = Text(label, font_size=18, color=WHITE).move_to(head.get_center())
            smile = Arc(radius=0.15, start_angle=-TAU/4 - 0.5, angle=1.0, color=WHITE).shift(DOWN*0.05)
            return VGroup(head, name, smile)

        alice = create_person(COLOR_ALICE, "A")
        bob = create_person(COLOR_BOB, "B")
        
        # Shares (fragments of necklace)
        share_a = Line(LEFT*0.4, RIGHT*0.4, color=WHITE).add(Dot(LEFT*0.2, color=RED, radius=0.05), Dot(RIGHT*0.2, color=GREEN, radius=0.05))
        share_b = Line(LEFT*0.4, RIGHT*0.4, color=WHITE).add(Dot(LEFT*0.2, color=YELLOW, radius=0.05), Dot(RIGHT*0.2, color=BLUE, radius=0.05))
        
        alice_total = VGroup(alice, share_a).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        bob_total = VGroup(bob, share_b).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        thieves_group = VGroup(alice_total, bob_total).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        self.place_in_area(thieves_group, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeIn(alice_total), FadeIn(bob_total))
        self.wait(1)

        # Final cohesive summary: Highlight the link between everything
        summary_link = Arrow(geom_group.get_bottom(), thieves_group.get_top(), color=GREY_A, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(summary_link))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clean up highlights for final shot
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fairness in Topology: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem and the Stolen Necklace Problem
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics or Computer Science

sections.title: The Hook: The Disputed Treasure
sections.content: Introduce a scenario where two thieves, Alice and Bob, have stolen a necklace made of different types of precious beads (e.g., rubies and emeralds). They want to split the necklace so that each person receives exactly half of each type of bead. The challenge is to find the minimum number of cuts required to achieve this 'fair split'.
sections.example: Visualize a long string with 10 red beads and 8 green beads arranged randomly. How can we cut it so Alice and Bob both get 5 red and 4 green?

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Intermediate Value Theorem (1D Case)
sections.content: Before tackling the necklace, introduce the 1D version of the logic. If a continuous function changes from a negative value to a positive value, it must pass through zero. This ensures that on a continuous 'sliding scale' of a cut, there is always a point of perfect 50/50 balance for one type of bead.
sections.example: An animation of a knife sliding along a string of only red beads. At the start, Alice has 0%; at the end, she has 100%. Therefore, there must be a spot in the middle where she has exactly 50%.

sections.title: The Core Concept: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
sections.content: Define the theorem formally but visually: For any continuous map from an n-sphere (Sn) to Euclidean n-space (Rn), there exists at least one pair of antipodal points (points exactly opposite each other on the sphere) that map to the same value.
sections.example: The 'Earth Example': At any given moment, there are two points exactly opposite each other on Earth's surface that have the exact same temperature and the exact same barometric pressure.

sections.title: Mapping the Necklace to a Sphere
sections.content: Explain how a necklace with 'k' types of beads can be represented as a mathematical space. We represent the possible cutting positions as coordinates on a high-dimensional sphere. A point on this sphere represents a specific way to partition the necklace between Alice and Bob.
sections.example: A 3D animation showing a circular necklace being projected onto a sphere, where moving to the 'opposite' side of the sphere represents giving Bob everything Alice previously had, and vice-versa.

sections.title: The Elegant Solution
sections.content: Apply Borsuk-Ulam to the necklace. If there are 'k' types of beads, we map the sphere to R^k (where each dimension is the amount of one bead type Alice receives). The theorem guarantees a pair of antipodal points with the same value. Since antipodal points represent a total swap of shares, the only way they can be 'equal' is if both shares are exactly 50/50.
sections.example: Show a necklace with 2 types of beads. By the theorem, only 2 cuts are needed. The animation shows the cuts shifting until the 'balance' function for both bead types hits the zero-difference point simultaneously.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-World Intuition
sections.content: Summarize that for 'k' types of beads, 'k' cuts are always sufficient. Highlight how topology—a study of shapes—provides a definitive answer to a problem of discrete fairness and resource allocation.
sections.example: Final shot of Alice and Bob walking away happy with their perfectly equal shares, overlaid with a geometric grid showing the 'path to fairness' on a sphere.
